scope_boundary: TU/MU measurement is prerequisite to utility-based individual demand, not evidence the same examination action is performed.
Meaning of the budget line differs from explaining why the budget line moves.
A shifted/rotated constraint does not prove mastery of substitution and income effects of different types of goods.
Defining productive/allocative efficiency and applying their conditions are different cognitive operations.
Returns to scale are production relationships; the LRAC curve and minimum efficient scale are cost relationships.
An owner–manager incentive conflict is not the same as identifying survival, sales, revenue or profit-satisficing objectives.
MR=MC profit-maximising logic must not automatically validate short- and long-run firm outcomes across market structures.
Identifying wage/nonwage determinants does not itself demonstrate correct shift-vs-movement graph interpretation.
National-income equilibrium/full-employment gaps and actual-versus-potential output gaps are closely related but have different scope/context.
Reading patterns and trends differs from evaluating unemployment policies.
How fixed/managed systems determine/maintain rates differs from explaining changes across regimes.
Explaining exchange-rate movements is not the same as explaining external effects via Marshall–Lerner and J-curve.
Distinct institutions and functions; do not merge merely because both concern development finance.
Cost-benefit reasoning is a general decision analysis; individual intervention policy instruments are separate assessed capabilities.
